title: Restriction preserves the augmented finite Cech tensor complex
statement: Let C be a small category with Grothendieck topology J, O a sheaf of commutative rings, r a natural number (possibly zero), and b a Fin r-indexed list of global sections of O. Assume unbounded derived categories of O-module sheaves on C and on every slice. Use the augmented complexes, slice lists and exact derived restriction functors of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system], and write Q for localization of complexes. For each object U, restricting the arrow Q(C_b→O[0]) to C/U gives an arrow isomorphic to Q(C_(b|U)→(O/U)[0]). For each morphism f:V→U, further restriction along Over.map f gives the analogous arrow for b|V. Each arrow isomorphism includes both source and ring-complex components and preserves the actual augmentation.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JB, lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U; algebraization.tex Tag 0996, lemma-map-twice-localize, and Tag 099E, lemma-global-extended-cech-complex

proof.text: 1. Restriction of sheaf modules is additive and preserves small colimits, since its underlying abelian-sheaf restriction is a cocontinuous inverse image and the forgetful functor reflects colimits. The natural module tensor restriction isomorphism extends to total complexes by the map-bifunctor comparison.

2. Induct on the ordered finite list. The base is the degree-zero ring complex with its identity augmentation. For the successor, tensor the arrow isomorphism of one localization factor with the induction hypothesis. Naturality of tensor restriction gives an arrow isomorphism; compose its codomain with the actual tensor unit isomorphisms on the two sites.

3. Apply Q to the resulting chain-level arrow isomorphism and the canonical factorization of exact restriction through Q. Repeat for Over.map f. The twice restricted sections are definitionally the original sections evaluated at the same domains.

proof_origin.note: Separated from the normalized comparison existence argument; finite-complex and categorical glue are written explicitly in Lean.

theorem exists_ringed_augmented_cech_restriction :
    (∀ U : C, Nonempty
      (Arrow.mk ((ringedDerivedRestriction O U).map
          (DerivedCategory.Q.map (ringedExtendedCech O r b).2)) ≅
        Arrow.mk (DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (ringedExtendedCech (O.over U) r
            (fun i ↦ ringedKoszulSliceSection O (b i) U)).2))) ∧
    (∀ (U V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), Nonempty
      (Arrow.mk ((ringedKoszulDerivedOverMap O f).map
          (DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (ringedExtendedCech (O.over U) r
              (fun i ↦ ringedKoszulSliceSection O (b i) U)).2)) ≅
        Arrow.mk (DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (ringedExtendedCech (O.over V) r
            (fun i ↦ ringedKoszulSliceSection O (b i) V)).2)))
